QuestionText: The default file extension for MS Word 2016/2019 documents is
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: MS Word 2007 and later saves files in .docx format (XML-based). Older .doc format is for Word 97-2003.

QuestionText: The keyboard shortcut to save a document is
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Ctrl+S saves the current document. Ctrl+P = Print, Ctrl+Z = Undo, Ctrl+C = Copy.

QuestionText: The keyboard shortcut to undo the last action is
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action. Ctrl+Y redoes.

QuestionText: In MS Word, the 'Find and Replace' dialogue is opened with
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Ctrl+H opens Find and Replace. Ctrl+F opens just Find.

QuestionText: The tool used to check spelling and grammar in MS Word is on the
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Spelling & Grammar check is in the Review tab. Shortcut: F7.

QuestionText: Mail Merge in MS Word is used to
Options: A) Create personalised letters/emails for many recipients at once
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Mail Merge combines a template document with a data source (Excel/Access) to create personalised documents for each record.

QuestionText: Styles in MS Word allow you to
Options: A) Apply consistent formatting to text with one click
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Styles (Heading 1, Normal, etc.) apply a set of formatting attributes (font, size, colour, spacing) in one click for consistency.

QuestionText: In MS Excel, cells are identified by
Options: A) Column letter and row number (e.g. B3)
B) Row number and column letter (e.g. 3B)
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Cell reference: Column letter + Row number. B3 = column B, row 3.

QuestionText: The formula to add values in cells A1 to A5 in Excel is
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: SUM function: =SUM(A1:A5) adds all values from A1 to A5. The colon (:) denotes a range.

QuestionText: In Excel, all formulas begin with
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Excel formulas must start with = to tell Excel it is a formula, not text.

QuestionText: The Excel function to find the average of cells B1:B10 is
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: AVERAGE: =AVERAGE(range) calculates the arithmetic mean of the values in the range.

QuestionText: The Excel function that returns the largest value in a range is
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: MAX returns the largest (maximum) value in a given range of cells.

QuestionText: The Excel function that counts only non-empty cells is
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: COUNTA counts non-empty cells (any data type). COUNT counts only cells containing numbers.

QuestionText: In Excel, the $ sign in a cell reference (e.g. $B$3) makes it
Options: A) Absolute (does not change when copied)
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Absolute reference ($B$3): stays fixed when formula is copied. Relative (B3): adjusts when copied. Mixed: $B3 or B$3.

QuestionText: A pie chart in Excel is best used to show
Options: A) How parts contribute to a whole (percentages)
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Pie chart: shows proportional parts of a whole. Best for showing percentages of a total with few categories.

QuestionText: A line chart is best used to show
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Line chart: ideal for showing data that changes over time (sales per month, temperature over days).

QuestionText: A bar/column chart is best used for
Options: A) Comparing values across different categories
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Bar/column charts compare discrete categories side by side (sales by region, scores by subject).

QuestionText: VLOOKUP in Excel is used to
Options: A) Look up a value in the first column of a table and return a value from another column
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: VLOOKUP(lookup_value, table_array, col_index_num, [range_lookup]): searches vertically in a table.

QuestionText: In Excel, the IF function syntax is
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: IF: =IF(A1>10, "Pass", "Fail") returns 'Pass' if A1>10, otherwise 'Fail'.

QuestionText: In MS PowerPoint, a 'slide transition' is
Options: A) An animation effect when moving from one slide to the next
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Slide transition: the visual effect that occurs when advancing from one slide to the next (fade, wipe, fly-in).

QuestionText: Animation in PowerPoint applies to
Options: A) Objects within a single slide (text, images)
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Animations (entrance, emphasis, exit, motion paths) apply to individual elements ON a slide (not between slides).

QuestionText: The Slide Master in PowerPoint is used to
Options: A) Set consistent formatting and layout for all slides
B) Add text to one slide
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Slide Master: controls the overall theme, fonts, colours, backgrounds, and layout applied to all slides from one place.

QuestionText: In PowerPoint, 'Presenter View' shows
Options: A) Speaker notes and upcoming slides visible only to the presenter
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Presenter View: the presenter sees current slide + notes + next slide on their screen; audience sees only the full-screen slide.

QuestionText: In MS Word, a 'Table of Contents' is automatically generated using
Options: A) Heading styles applied to sections
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Word generates TOC from text formatted with Heading styles (Heading 1, 2, 3). Insert > Table of Contents.

QuestionText: The Excel function COUNTIF counts cells
Options: A) That meet a specified condition
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: COUNTIF(range, criteria): counts cells in a range that satisfy a given condition. E.g. =COUNTIF(A1:A10, ">50").

QuestionText: The shortcut Ctrl+B in Word/Excel makes text
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Ctrl+B = Bold. Ctrl+I = Italic. Ctrl+U = Underline.

QuestionText: In Excel, to freeze the top row so it stays visible when scrolling, use
Options: A) View > Freeze Panes > Freeze Top Row
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Freeze Panes in the View tab keeps selected rows/columns visible while scrolling through large datasets.

QuestionText: The Excel function CONCATENATE (or &) is used to
Options: A) Join two or more text strings into one
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: CONCATENATE(A1," ",B1) or A1&" "&B1 joins text strings. In newer Excel: CONCAT function.

QuestionText: In MS Word, 'Track Changes' is used to
Options: A) Record edits so reviewers can see, accept, or reject them
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Track Changes: records every addition, deletion, and format change; useful for collaborative document editing.

QuestionText: A 'Header' in MS Word is text that
Options: A) Appears at the top of every page (e.g. document title, page number)
B) Appears only on the first page
C) Is the largest text on a page
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Headers appear at the top of every page; footers at the bottom. Useful for page numbers, dates, and titles.

QuestionText: Conditional Formatting in Excel allows you to
Options: A) Automatically format cells based on their values
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Conditional Formatting: applies formatting (colour, icons, data bars) to cells automatically based on rules/conditions.

QuestionText: The keyboard shortcut Ctrl+A in Office applications
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Ctrl+A selects all: all text in Word, all cells in Excel, all objects in PowerPoint.

QuestionText: Which Excel function rounds a number to a specified number of decimal places?
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: ROUND(3.14159, 2) = 3.14. ROUNDUP always rounds up; ROUNDDOWN always rounds down.

QuestionText: The 'Normal view' in PowerPoint shows
Options: A) The editing view with slide panel, main slide, and notes pane
D) A thumbnail of all slides
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Normal view: main editing view in PowerPoint showing the slide, thumbnails panel, and notes pane.

QuestionText: A 'Macro' in Excel/Word is
Options: A) A recorded sequence of actions that can be replayed automatically
D) A type of cell reference
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Macros automate repetitive tasks by recording a sequence of commands and replaying them with a single keystroke or button.

QuestionText: In Excel, a PivotTable is used to
Options: A) Summarise, analyse, and explore large datasets interactively
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: PivotTable: powerful tool that lets you drag-and-drop fields to group, filter, and aggregate large datasets without formulas.

QuestionText: The Excel function SUMIF adds values
Options: A) That meet a specified condition
B) That are all values in a range
C) That are even numbers only
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range): sums cells that meet the condition. E.g. total sales for a specific region.

QuestionText: In PowerPoint, the '5-6-7 rule' for slide design suggests
Options: A) 5-6 lines per slide, 6-7 words per line, to avoid information overload
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: The 5-6-7 rule (and similar '6×6 rule'): limit bullet points and words per slide to keep slides readable and not text-heavy.

QuestionText: In Excel, entering a date as text (e.g. 'Jan 2024') vs a real date value matters because
Options: A) Real date values allow date calculations; text entries do not
C) Real dates take more space
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Excel stores dates as serial numbers; only real date values support date arithmetic (DATEDIF, NETWORKDAYS, etc.).

QuestionText: The function key F5 in PowerPoint
Options: A) Starts the slide show from the beginning
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: F5 starts the slide show from the first slide. Shift+F5 starts from the current slide.

QuestionText: In Word, a 'section break' allows
Options: A) Different formatting (margins, orientation, columns) in different parts of the document
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Section breaks divide a document into independently formatted sections, each with its own page layout settings.

QuestionText: In Excel, the '#REF!' error means
Options: A) A cell reference is invalid (referenced cell was deleted)
C) Value is text not number
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: #REF! error: a formula references a cell that no longer exists (e.g. a row was deleted that a formula pointed to).

QuestionText: In Excel, the '#DIV/0!' error means
Options: A) Division by zero occurred in the formula
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: #DIV/0!: a formula attempts to divide by zero or by an empty cell.

QuestionText: In Word, 'AutoCorrect' automatically
Options: A) Corrects common spelling mistakes and typos as you type
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: AutoCorrect: automatically fixes common typos and misspellings as you type (e.g. 'teh' → 'the').

QuestionText: The Word Count feature in MS Word is found in the
Options: A) Review tab (or in the status bar at the bottom)
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Word Count (Review > Word Count or the status bar at the bottom) shows words, characters, paragraphs, and pages.

QuestionText: In Excel, data validation is used to
Options: A) Restrict the type or range of data entered in a cell
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Data Validation: controls what data can be entered in a cell (e.g. only integers between 1-100, or a dropdown list).

QuestionText: The 'SmartArt' feature in Office is used to
Options: A) Create visually appealing diagrams (processes, hierarchies, cycles)
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: SmartArt: Insert > SmartArt allows creation of professional diagrams — process flows, org charts, Venn diagrams, etc.

QuestionText: A 'theme' in PowerPoint applies
Options: A) Consistent colours, fonts, and effects to the entire presentation
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Themes: pre-designed sets of colours, fonts, and graphic effects that give presentations a professional, consistent look.

QuestionText: To insert a hyperlink in Word or PowerPoint, use the shortcut
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Ctrl+K opens the Insert Hyperlink dialog in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

QuestionText: Iterating through data with Excel's 'fill handle' means
Options: A) Dragging the small square at the bottom-right of a cell to auto-fill a series
Topic: Computer - MS Office Word Excel PowerPoint
Explanation: Fill handle: drag the small square at cell's bottom-right to copy/extend patterns (dates, numbers, formulas) to adjacent cells.
